//: Documented divergences from the reference engines, read by validation/grid/compare.R when it compares parameters against an oracle (gate 2) or Satterthwaite df against lmerTest (gate 5, quantity coef_df, in the glmm-vs-oracle scope) and when it scores truth error (gate 3), and by the in-crate goldens tier (tests/oracle_support) for entries scoped to it. Gate 3 judges a group of cells -- one family, estimator arm and quantity -- so there an entry on any cell of the group covers the whole group, and is stale when the group was scored and did not need it. The rules: a difference over band with no entry here FAILS; a difference over band that an entry covers is reported as DOC and passes; a difference that has grown past its entry's max_rel FAILS, so a divergence is never silently absorbed; and an entry whose cell was compared but whose divergence did not fire FAILS as stale, so this file lists only what is still true. `summary` is the standalone short form, so an entry means something without the long form.
//fields: id: stable key. cell: which fixture -- a grid cell id for the grid's own consumers, a golden's or an inference reference's name for an 'oracle-tier' entry. comparison: 'glmm-vs-oracle' for a glmm-against-an-oracle difference, 'glmm-vs-truth' for a truth-gate group where glmm's mean error against the generating truth is above the best oracle's by more than the band, 'oracle-tier' for the in-crate oracle-tests tiers (the goldens and the inference references); an entry may list several. quantities: the comparison labels each consumer uses. max_rel: the largest relative difference the entry covers (the largest absolute difference for a quantity its consumer compares absolutely, such as the oracle tier's 'lrt'; for 'glmm-vs-truth', the largest amount by which glmm's mean truth error may sit above the best oracle's plus the band) — an observation exceeding it FAILS, so a divergence that grows is not silently absorbed. direction: which way the criterion moved.
//scope: Every entry here is an oracle defect, a parameter the data does not determine, or, in the oracle tier only, one of two kinds that need extra support. (a) An oracle that maximises a different objective from glmm's: admitted only where the comparison cannot move to a twin on glmm's own objective, and only when such a twin (a glmmTMB `_tmb` golden, or the population-mode rows of the same reference's glmmTMB block) is gated at the ordinary bands in the same tier. The goldens tier compares the parameters of such an lme4 golden on its twin alone, so it needs no entry. (b) A convention difference, where the oracle reports another named quantity at its fit (another covariance or information matrix): admitted only when the entry names both conventions and either the same tier gates glmm's own computation of the oracle's convention at the ordinary bands (as the `WaldSe::Rx` refit is gated against lme4's `se.fit`), or, where glmm has no switch for it, the entry records a closed-form check that reproduces each side's values to round-off. A real glmm defect is never registered — it stays red and is tracked as a bug — because an entry would let it pass.

entries.direction: glmm's fourth crossed SD is 3.9e-03 relative below glmmTMB's (0.15416 against 0.15477) at the same optimum; glmm holds the lower deviance by 7.4e-06
entries.summary: glmmTMB is the only converged oracle on glmm's objective here (lme4 fits a different objective on Gamma). The two engines reach the same optimum, glmm's deviance 7.4e-06 lower. Three of the six crossed random-intercept SDs are 0 there (glmm exactly 0, glmmTMB 2.8e-07, 8.2e-06 and 1.1e-03, below sd_boundary_abs), and the fourth differs by 3.9e-03 relative inside the same deviance gap: the likelihood is flat along these components and the data do not determine the fourth to the 1e-03 band. Measured 2026-09-26; 3.92e-03 re-measured 2026-10-27 on the kept 0.7.0 run against the glmmTMB run of 2026-10-27.

entries.summary: Same kind as gami_cross6_g3000p20_bal_base. glmmTMB is the only converged oracle on glmm's objective here (lme4 fits a different objective on Gamma). entries.direction: glmm's intercept is 8.2e-06 above glmmTMB's; glmm holds the lower deviance by 5.7e-09
entries.summary: The estimated intercept is 0.0022 and its standard error is 0.13, sixty times larger, so the data do not determine it to the 1e-03 relative band: that band asks for agreement to 2.2e-06, which is 1.7e-05 standard errors. glmm and glmmTMB differ by 8.2e-06, which is 6.2e-05 standard errors. On a quadratic surface that costs 3.9e-09 deviance units, which matches the measured 5.7e-09 gap and is below what either optimizer resolves. The slope agrees to 3.2e-07. lme4 and MixedModels fit a different objective on this cloglog cell and are not references. Measured 2026-09-26 on the accuracy grid.

entries.direction: glmm's correlation is exactly 1 and GLMMadaptive's 0.999995; under GLMMadaptive's own quadrature rule glmm's estimates hold the lower deviance by 1.2e-04
entries.summary: On this cell glmm puts the two-term g1 block on the boundary, with correlation exactly 1. GLMMadaptive stops at 0.999995 and warns that its Hessian at convergence is not positive definite. Evaluated under GLMMadaptive's own quadrature rule at glmm's estimates, with the correlation taken toward 1, the deviance is 78.59599802: 1.2e-04 below GLMMadaptive's reported optimum (78.59611657) and equal to glmm's own deviance to 4e-12. So GLMMadaptive stops short of its own optimum. The differences are 3.2e-03 on beta, 5.0e-02 on se_hessian and 7.5e-02 on the intercept SD (0.0589 against 0.0545); the slope SD agrees to 8e-04. GLMMadaptive is the only oracle on the AGQ arm for this cell. Measured 2026-10-05 against the 2026-10-05 grid run, GLMMadaptive run of 2026-10-05.

entries.direction: glmm's p is exactly 1 (its pinned fit gives a statistic of exactly 0, so no null is drawn); RLRsim's is 0.4392, a simulation on a statistic of 5.68e-14
entries.summary: On Dyestuff2 the between-batch variance is estimated at exactly 0: lme4 reports a singular fit at theta = 0 and glmm pins the component. lme4's REML logLik then equals logLik(lm, REML = TRUE) to the last digit (-80.914138906144217 both in R 4.5.3 with lme4 2.0-6, checked 2026-10-12; the frozen rlrt_dyestuff2.json stores 15 digits, -80.9141389061442), but RLRsim's exactRLRT recomputes the theta = 0 value through its own QR (reml.H0) and takes the difference, 5.68e-14 (2^-44, round-off). That is not 0, so it simulates and reports p = mean(5.68e-14 < sample) = 0.4392 (nsim 1e5, set.seed(20261002)), one minus the share of its null's draws that are exactly 0 (56080 of 1e5). The exact p-value at a zero statistic is 1, and RLRsim itself gives 1 without simulating when its statistic is exactly 0. glmm's statistic agrees with RLRsim's within the statistic's band (4e-6), so only the p-value is registered: |1 - 0.4392| / 0.4392 = 1.2769, an oracle defect. Measured 2026-10-12 against the frozen rlrt_dyestuff2.json.

entries.direction: glmm's deviance is 0.0243 above lme4's reported one, which is not the same function of the parameters; glmm's agrees with glmmTMB's (sim_nb_glmm_tmb) to 1.2e-09
entries.summary: The larger model of this pair is lme4's glmer.nb fit of y ~ 1 + x + grp + (1 | cluster) on sim_nb, the model of the goldens tier's sim_nb_glmm. lme4's glmer.nb builds the Laplace log-determinant from the expected (Fisher) weight, which on the negative-binomial log link is not the curvature of the integrand at the mode, so its logLik is not the Laplace approximation glmm and glmmTMB maximise. The smaller model (MASS::glm.nb) agrees with glmm to 1.7e-12 in deviance, so the comparison carries the whole gap. The deviance gate reads the glmer.nb side against the frozen glmmTMB fit of the same model instead (sim_nb_glmm_tmb, gap 1.2e-09). glmm's likelihood-ratio statistic is 31.71512 against lme4's 31.73942, an absolute difference of 0.0243 (the quantity lrt is compared absolutely). Measured 2026-10-12.

entries.direction: glmm's conditional-mode standard errors are above lme4's on every over-band row (0.805618 against 0.771295 on the worst row); glmm's default fit reads the Hessian covariance of the fixed effects, lme4's se.fit the RX one
entries.summary: lme4's predict(se.fit = TRUE) builds the fixed-effect part of the standard error from vcov_full, the RX (expected-information) covariance, even on a fit whose vcov() is the Hessian one; glmm's default fit (WaldSe::Hessian) uses the Hessian covariance of the joint (theta, beta) Laplace deviance. On this binomial GLMM the two differ by up to 0.10 relative on the diagonal (lme4's own vcov(use.hessian = TRUE) against use.hessian = FALSE). glmmTMB's conditional se.fit is a third convention: it adds the uncertainty of the variance parameter on seen levels and the prior variance of the effect on unseen ones, so it is no nearer. 58 conditional-mode lines are over the band (both scales), from 1.13e-03 to 4.45e-02 relative to the nearer reference; the worst rows are the unseen-level rows 5 and 17. Population-mode standard errors pass against glmmTMB. The same driver refits under WaldSe::Rx and gates that fit's se.fit against lme4's at the ordinary band, hard: worst 1.6e-04 relative, so the formula is lme4's and only the covariance differs. Measured 2026-10-26 against the frozen predict_glmm_sim_factorial_bern.json.

entries.direction: the worst rows are unseen-level rows, where glmm's standard error is above lme4's (0.32079 against 0.28186 on row 8, response scale); glmm's estimates are maximum likelihood, lme4's are not
entries.summary: On a Gamma GLMM lme4's glmer does not maximise the Laplace likelihood over the dispersion: it plugs in its pwrss/n scale, so its estimates are not maximum likelihood (random-intercept variance 0.2354 against glmm's 0.3225, phi 0.5726 against 0.5391; glmmTMB agrees with glmm to six digits). On the four unseen-level rows (2, 5, 8, 11) lme4's conditional se.fit is its population one, x'Vx, at those estimates: evaluated at glmm's estimates the same formula moves from 0.12283 to 0.13571 on row 8, against glmm's 0.13640, the small rest being the RX covariance lme4 reads in place of glmm's Hessian one. glmmTMB adds the prior variance of the new effect there, so it is no nearer (0.58407). In population mode glmm and glmmTMB agree to six digits and pass. The seen-level conditional rows fall under this entry too, because the registry is keyed by reference and quantity: there lme4's conditional variance is the expected-information one (see oracle-predict-glmm-sim-gamma-condvar-lme4-expected-information) and glmmTMB's se.fit adds the uncertainty of the variance parameter, up to 2.13e-02 relative to the nearer reference. 18 lines over the band, from 1.19e-03 to 1.381e-01 relative; the worst is unseen row 8 on the response scale. Measured 2026-10-26 against the frozen predict_glmm_sim_gamma.json.

entries.direction: glmm's conditional variances spread around lme4's single value (0.03467 to 0.04644 against 0.03967 on every level); glmm uses the observed information of each level's effect, lme4 the expected one
entries.summary: lme4's ranef(condVar = TRUE) on a GLMM is the expected-information conditional variance, 1/(1/sigma_b^2 + n_j/phi) on a Gamma log-link random intercept: it reproduces lme4's postVar to 6.9e-18, and it is one value for every level of the same size (all 24 clusters have 12 rows, so lme4 reports 0.03967 on each). glmm's condvar is the inverse of the observed curvature of the Laplace integrand at the mode, which depends on each level's data; it matches the observed-information formula to 4.4e-16. On the canonical-link entries (binomial logit, Poisson log) the two coincide and pass; on Gamma's log link they do not. lme4's estimates are also not maximum likelihood here (see oracle-predict-glmm-sim-gamma-se-fit-lme4-estimates), which adds to the gap. 44 lines over the band (22 postVar entries, 22 condsd), from 4.46e-03 to 1.704e-01 relative; the worst is cluster 10's postVar. Measured 2026-10-26 against the frozen predict_glmm_sim_gamma.json.

entries.direction: lme4's conditional-mode standard errors are wrong in both directions (2.37542 against the exact 0.57250 on row 1, 0.70638 against 1.11555 on row 7); glmm's are the exact joint value
entries.summary: On Pastes (strength ~ 1 + (1 | batch/cask)) lme4 2.0-6's predict(se.fit = TRUE) has two defects. vcov_full rebuilds the joint covariance from RZX without the fill-reducing permutation P of the sparse factor, while RZX is permuted, so its covariance is wrong whenever P is not the identity (4.2 off the exact joint inverse here, in the largest entry; on the balanced Penicillin, where vcov_full matches, RZX is the same with or without P). And predict.merMod pairs the columns of the new data's Z with the rows of that covariance by position, not by level, so a row reads another level's variance. glmm's se.fit on the seen rows is 0.5725015 against the exact full-joint value 0.5725018 at lme4's own parameters. glmmTMB adds the uncertainty of the variance parameters, and the prior variance on new levels, so it is up to 2.1e-03 off the exact value on the seen rows and far off on the new-level rows. 10 conditional-mode lines over the band (both scales), from 1.286e-03 to 5.793e-01 relative to the nearer reference; the worst is row 7 (batch A, a new cask). Population mode passes. An oracle defect, recorded in reference_disagreements.md section 2. Measured 2026-10-26 against the frozen predict_pastes.json.
